input.prompt: Lo-fi Hayes Valley. DJ Soft Launch here. Take a breath. The email can develop a personality without you.
That was another little afternoon from our record shelf. Your shoulders are not responsible for the entire company.
If the fog hides your destination, enjoy having fewer tabs open in real life. Bring a layer.
Lo-fi Hayes Valley. Your calendar has a gap. Please do not immediately pave it.
West Coast Tech Radio. Pat Pending, opinions with no liquidation preference. Every company on this show is fictional. Several of the business models are too.
You are listening to West Coast Tech Radio. Callers receive one unsolicited opinion and absolutely no investment advice.
Time for our weather desk. It is San Francisco. Bring a jacket and stop asking the cloud for a valuation.
West Coast Tech Radio. Back after these entirely fictional sponsors. Nobody has paid us. This will be obvious.

This Tech Week, dress for the round you want. Vested Interest brings you the sleeveless jacket with twelve pockets for twelve different conference badges. Breathable fabric. Unbreathable valuation. Now with a tiny pocket for your remaining equity. Vested Interest. A fictional product for a very real temperature problem.

Still lying awake wondering if your startup should become something else? Try the Pivot Pillow. Turn it over and discover a completely new business model. The cool side is enterprise. The other side is community. Pivot Pillow. Sleep on it, then rebrand it. Fictional bedding. Actual exhaustion sold separately.

Deck Dusters cleans the slide nobody understands. We remove jargon, polish your hockey stick, and put a little sparkle on the word platform. Our premium service replaces your entire strategy with one tasteful gradient. Deck Dusters. A fictional cleaning company for very dusty pitch decks. Results may contain whitespace.

Your company has six months of runway. Your lunch has three minutes. Runway Noodles. The fictional instant meal with a burn rate you can actually afford. Just add hot water and one achievable milestone. Now available in Seed Broth and Series A Spicy. Please do not pitch the kettle.

Introducing Meeting Meadow. The fictional calendar app that replaces every unnecessary meeting with a picture of grass. Your weekly sync is now a fern. Your alignment session is a small pond. Meeting Meadow. Touch grass without adding another recurring appointment. No lawn care expertise required. Silence is our premium feature.

Too many Tech Week events and only one neck? Badge Barge is the fictional conference lanyard with industrial suspension. Carry every credential you have ever earned, plus three you found near the snacks. Badge Barge. Network harder, stand slightly differently. Not suitable for swimming, sleeping, or modest doorways.

Today on the Pat Pending show: moats. A caller from a fictional startup says their competitive moat is a spreadsheet only one employee understands. Congratulations. That is not a moat. That is a bus factor wearing a blazer. The caller says they have added artificial intelligence. Excellent. Now two things do not understand the spreadsheet. My producer wants to know our own moat. We broadcast from a room with a door that sticks. Nobody can acquire us because nobody can get in. Coming up: a founder who describes charging money as an exciting experiment. Stay with West Coast Tech Radio.

We have a caller from a Tech Week coffee queue. Caller, what are you building? Apparently a queue for people waiting to join other queues. There is a premium tier that lets you see the queue. Beautiful. A marketplace with both sides standing still. How many customers? The caller says everyone ahead of them. That is an addressable market, not a customer list. My producer has joined the queue. We have lost the producer. If you see someone holding a microphone and explaining network effects to a pastry, please send them back. This is West Coast Tech Radio.

Welcome back. A fictional founder has sent us a demo with three buttons. The first button says coming soon. The second says request access. The third opens a calendar. Finally, a product with measurable meeting fit. The founder tells me the demo worked yesterday. Yesterday is not available for comment. We invited the engineer, who asked whether we could simply turn the radio off and on again. We tried that, and our audience doubled from one to two. Both are the engineer. After the break, we investigate whether a rooftop mixer is just a very expensive way to find the stairs.

Our topic is exit strategies. Listener number one says their exit strategy is leaving the networking event before anyone asks what they do. Sensible. Listener number two has located a side door near the snacks. Strong execution. Listener number three is still saying goodbye forty minutes later. That is a lockup period. Here at West Coast Tech Radio, our own exit is clearly marked and occasionally blocked by a box of promotional tote bags. Remember, a successful evening does not have to include a term sheet. Sometimes you meet a nice person, eat something warm, and catch the right bus. Pat Pending, signing off this segment.
